title: Commas with yes, no, and names
keyIdea: Use a comma to set off a word that stands apart from the rest of the sentence. Put a comma after yes or no when it is a reply (Yes, I understand). Set off the name of the person you are speaking to, which is called direct address: one comma at the start or end (Sarah, please pass the salt; Thank you, Ben) and a pair in the middle (I think, Mum, that we are late). Put a comma before a tag question and a question mark after it (It's cold today, isn't it?). If yes, no or a name is just part of the sentence (No dogs are allowed; I told Ben), it gets no comma.
familyTip: Read a text message or a bit of dialogue together and hunt for names. Ask: is this person being spoken to, or just talked about? Only the person spoken to gets a comma. Then swap a sentence around, Mum, can you help? to Can you help, Mum?, and watch the comma follow the name.

visual.caption: Does it need a comma? Drag each card, or tap it and then tap a box.

lab.caption: Flagship lab: find who is spoken to, tap where commas go, punctuate tag questions, sort comma or no comma, and move a name through a sentence.

kid: A comma can set off a word that stands apart. Yes and no often do this. Yes, I understand. No, thank you.
You also set off the name of the person you talk to. Sam, come here. Thank you, Ben. If the name is in the middle, it needs a comma on each side: I think, Mum, that we are late.
A tag question is a little question on the end, like isn't it. Put a comma before it and a question mark at the end: It's cold today, isn't it?
Be careful. Sam came here has no comma, because nobody is spoken to. No dogs are allowed has no comma, because no means not any.
adult: Ages 10 to 11. Common Core L.5.2c covers three comma jobs. Use a comma to set off yes and no. Use one to set off a tag question. Use one to show direct address (Is that you, Steve?). In England, Years 5 and 6 use commas to make meaning clear. This builds on commas in lists, after fronted adverbials and in speech.

The grammar. Yes and no as a reply are interjections. They sit outside the main clause, so a comma sets them off. A name in direct address is called a vocative. It names the person spoken to. It is not the subject or object of the verb. It takes one comma at the start or end, and a pair in the middle. A tag question is a short question on the end, such as isn't it or can we. A comma marks the join, and the whole sentence ends with a question mark.

Common mistakes. Some children put a comma after every name, even a subject or object (Sam, came to look). Some leave out the second comma of a pair (I think, Mia you're right). Some put a comma after no when it means not any; No, dogs allowed says the opposite of the sign. Others split Thank you (Thank, you Leo) or end a tag question with a full stop.

In the lab your child finds who is spoken to in six sentences. They tap the gaps for commas in five. They drag a comma and a question mark into four tag questions. They sort eight sentences into needs a comma or no comma. Last, they move the name Zara to the start, middle and end of a sentence and place the commas each time.

practice.hint: Yes is a reply. Where does the comma go?
practice.explain: Yes is a reply that stands apart from the rest, so a comma goes straight after it: Yes, I can help.

practice.prompt: A letter has {a} names of people being spoken to in the middle of sentences and {b} at the start. How many commas do they need?
practice.hint: A name in the middle needs a pair. A name at the start needs one.
practice.explain: {a} names in the middle need 2 each, which is {=2*a}, and {b} at the start need 1 each. That makes {=2*a+b} commas.
In Sam came to look, Sam is the subject, not the person spoken to, so there is no comma. The other two speak to Sam.

practice.prompt: You write {n} tag questions, like It's cold, isn't it? How many commas and question marks do you use in total?
practice.hint: Each tag question has one comma and one question mark.
practice.explain: Each tag question needs a comma before the tag and a question mark at the end, so {n} of them need {=2*n} marks.

practice.prompt: Which is the tag question punctuated correctly?
practice.hint: A comma before the tag. What goes at the end of a question?
practice.explain: A comma joins the statement to the tag, and a tag question asks something, so it ends with a question mark.

pool.hint: A name in the middle needs a pair.
pool.explain: Mia is spoken to in the middle of the sentence, so she needs a comma on each side.

pool.prompt: A sign is meant to keep dogs out. Which is right?
pool.hint: Here no means not any dogs.
pool.explain: No is part of the phrase no dogs, so there is no comma. No, dogs allowed would mean dogs are allowed.

pool.hint: Thank you stays together. Who is spoken to?
pool.explain: Leo is the person spoken to, so a comma sets the name off from Thank you.

pool.prompt: Which one of these sentences has no comma job to do?
choices: She said no to the plan.
pool.hint: Is no a reply, or part of the sentence?
pool.explain: In She said no to the plan, no is what she said, inside the sentence. In the others yes and no are replies and need a comma.

choices: Naming the person you are speaking to
Using a name as the subject of a sentence
pool.explain: Direct address names the person spoken to, like Ben in Ben, you were right. That name is set off by commas.

pool.prompt: A story has {a} names spoken to at the start or end of sentences and {b} in the middle. How many commas do the names need?
pool.hint: Start or end: one comma. Middle: two.
pool.explain: {a} names need 1 comma each and {b} need 2 each ({=2*b}), so {=a+2*b} commas.

pool.prompt: A play script has {n} replies that start with yes or no. How many commas do those words need?
pool.hint: One comma straight after each yes or no reply.
pool.explain: Each reply word gets one comma after it, so {n} replies need {=n} commas.

pool.prompt: Where does the comma go? Is that you Grandad
pool.hint: Who is being spoken to in this question?
pool.explain: You are speaking to Grandad, so a comma sets the name off: Is that you, Grandad?

pool.prompt: Which tag question is punctuated correctly?
pool.hint: Comma before the tag, question mark at the end.
pool.explain: can we is a tag question, so a comma comes before it and a question mark ends the sentence.
